summary.short: Decree 699 adds two paragraphs to Article 185 Bis C of the Sinaloa Penal Code. Criminalises using AI to manipulate intimate sexual images, audio or video to create false facts appearing real and disseminate them without consent, with the penalties of the second paragraph. In force the day after publication.
summary.long: Decree 699 of the Sinaloa State Congress adds a fifth and sixth paragraph to Article 185 Bis C of the Sinaloa Penal Code, renumbering later paragraphs. The fifth paragraph applies the same penalties as the second paragraph to anyone who, using artificial intelligence, manipulates intimate sexual images, audio or video of a person to create false facts with apparent reality, in order to expose, distribute, disseminate, transmit, sell, offer or share them through print, email, telephone messages, social networks or other technological means, without the person's express, voluntary, genuine and desired consent. The sixth paragraph defines artificial intelligence as applications, programs or technology that analyse photographs, audio or video and offer automatic adjustments to alter or modify them. The text states no penalty amounts; it refers to the penalties of the second paragraph of the same article. Transitory articles set entry into force on the day after publication in the Periódico Oficial 'El Estado de Sinaloa' and repeal provisions that conflict with the decree. The masthead shows publication on 12 February 2024.

notes: Decree No. 699 adds paragraphs to article 185 Bis C of the Sinaloa penal code. Only the added text is in the document. The penalties the new paragraph refers to (the 'segundo párrafo' of the article) are not reproduced here, so no penalty is coded. The repeal clause does not identify the provisions it repeals. The decree names no firm and designates or empowers no authority; the issuing bodies appear only in the enacting formula. The relations section has entries, so its section_status is recorded as not_applicable with an explanation. The entry-into-force date is not given in the text; the publication date comes from the newspaper header (12 February 2024). The signature block of the scanned text is partly illegible.
